title: Mnesia Distributed DBMS: Tables, ACID Transactions & Rollback
solutionExplanation: Implements an atomic wallet ledger using Mnesia transactions with strict abort rollback semantics.

otpDocCards.description: Executes the functional closure Fun within an atomic, isolated Mnesia transaction with automatic rollback.
otpDocCards.complexityNote: Acquires row/table locks and buffers writes in transaction journal.

otpDocCards.description: Reads all records with Key from table Tab within the current transaction, acquiring read locks.
otpDocCards.complexityNote: O(1) hash lookup with lock acquisition.

otpDocCards.description: Writes Record into the table specified by element 1 of the record within the current transaction.
otpDocCards.complexityNote: Buffers modification in the local transaction store.

otpDocCards.description: Terminates the current transaction immediately, rolling back all buffered modifications and releasing locks.

mentalModelCheck.question: What occurs when a fun passed to mnesia:transaction/1 calls mnesia:abort(insufficient_funds) after having already written to another table?

options.label: The writes already completed remain committed, while subsequent writes are cancelled.
options.explanation: Mnesia transactions are atomic; partial commits are never allowed.

options.label: Mnesia pauses the node and writes the error to crash.dump.
options.explanation: Aborting a transaction is a normal operational event and does not crash the BEAM node.

options.label: 100% of writes inside that transaction are discarded and rolled back; no table changes are committed.
options.explanation: Mnesia transactions provide full ACID atomicity. If mnesia:abort/1 is called or an unhandled exception occurs, all writes buffered during that transaction are discarded and rolled back.

options.label: The transaction retries indefinitely until sufficient funds are deposited.
options.explanation: Transactions only retry on transient lock conflicts, not on explicit mnesia:abort/1.
